R378 — stock bench.sh longer-case settings audit
Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo)
Status: READ-ONLY source review and design note. No code edit, client/server invocation, test, import, model/GPU/process/service work, profiler, Git operation, or cleanup. This report is the only new artifact.

## Scope and inputs

Followed `round339-updated-xestrata-lifetime-and-fullcontext-safety-delta.txt`, R339’s upstream client/API route findings, and `docs/MEASUREMENT_WORKFLOW.md` from `feat-fixed-history-logits-comparator-20261013`. Reviewed pristine client U `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/Niko1221/Strata/.worktree/bench-upstream-v0143-pristine-20261012` (provided HEAD `7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d`): `bench.sh`, `tools/strata_bench.py`, and `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`. The engine worktree and active Main run were not read. No benchmark was run; this report does not claim that 64K/128/256 was measured.

## Finding: no existing setting for this workload

The stock wrapper forwards every argument unchanged to `tools/strata_bench.py` (`bench.sh:5-7`). Its CLI exposes `--long` as a boolean whose help text fixes the case at about 32,768 prompt tokens; it has no input-length or long-output-length option (`strata_bench.py:835-849`). The implementation uses `LONG_MAX_TOKENS = 24` for every prompt test (`:57`, `:281-302`), and `Suite.run()` selects only target `32768` for `--long` (`:401-411`). Thus the official `bench.sh` path has no supported argument/config/API way to ask this unchanged client for a 64K-class input or a 128/256-token long completion. The normal `/v1/chat/completions` request accepts the chosen `max_tokens`, but the client hardcodes it for this case; its current request body has no EOS-suppression option (`:128-139`).

This means the requested longer case cannot currently be selected by command-line flags, config, or API request parameters while leaving this client revision unchanged. Directly editing the constant or calling the Python class with custom arguments would cease to be the pristine stock invocation under review.

The existing prompt builder is a calibrated word-list generator: two small requests estimate tokens per word, then `prompt_for()` chooses a word count for a target (`:240-254`). The report must continue to use the server’s actual `usage.prompt_tokens` for each individual row; the target is approximate. The client already records actual completion count from API usage (falling back to streamed-piece count), prompt speed and decode speed separately, and median/min/max/n (`:178-201`, `:297-302`). It does not currently retain stream `finish_reason` (`:141-168`), so a short completion caused by EOS cannot be distinguished from hitting the token cap using its saved row alone.

## Minimal source-only extension proposal

Add two optional long-case settings to `tools/strata_bench.py`, passed through the unchanged wrapper:

- `--long-input-tokens N`, default `32768` when `--long` is selected.
- `--long-output-tokens N`, default `24` when `--long` is selected.

Keep `--long` required to include that case. Route only this selected long case through `run_prompt(input_target, label, output_cap)`; leave the existing 4K, 16K, chat, agent, and concurrency suite behavior/constants unchanged. Add the selected values to the result’s `params` and command string, and include them explicitly in the long prompt result. Preserve the existing request URL, streamed HTTP method, model name, temperature 0, thinking-off fields, prompt generator/calibration, timings source, and per-request rows. A representative invocation after such a small extension would be `./bench.sh --url http://127.0.0.1:18095 --long --long-input-tokens 65536 --long-output-tokens 128 --runs 3 --out DIR`; 256 would be a separate invocation/arm using the same client revision and server configuration.

This keeps the upstream client and measurement route central: changes are limited to optional case parameters and reporting. Defaults retain the stock `--long` case. Do not repurpose global `LONG_MAX_TOKENS`, because that would silently change the ordinary 4K/16K measurements and the published table’s stated cap. Do not change agent constants or its multi-turn session to make this long case.

## Comparison and result rules for the extension

- Keep each OFF/ON pair on the same client revision, binary/model/config, prompt target, output cap, run count, and server settings. Compare prefill and decode independently. For the 1000 tok/s prefill objective, use the same input target and compare per-request engine prompt tok/s; the 128/256 cap is a separate decode dimension. Run 128 and 256 as distinct matched arms, each with at least three rows. If decode spread overlaps enough to leave the decision unclear, increase repetitions for both compared arms under the same rule.
- Report actual prompt tokens for every row, not the target label. A request below 65,536 actual input tokens is still reported by its measured count; it does not establish a >=64K-input result. Keep the client’s calibrated prompt path and record that a target means “about N tokens.” The existing workflow’s rule for 32,049 actual tokens remains applicable.
- Preserve prompt-cache settings across arms and inspect actual `reused_tokens`/`read_tokens` for each row. For a fresh-prefill comparison, the server-side prompt cache must be disabled identically in both arms and measured rows should show zero reuse; the stock client’s unique prompt tag is helpful but is not proof of zero reuse. Do not silently pool reused and fresh rows. Keep any cache-metric anomaly and original row status in the report.
- `max_tokens` is an upper bound; the stock API path may finish at EOS before 128/256. Do not claim fixed generated work from the cap. Minimal extension should retain `completion_tokens` as actual work and also capture the streamed choice’s `finish_reason` in `chat()`/`digest()` so rows distinguish `length` from `stop`. Report actual completion count per row and summarize it alongside decode tok/s. Keep speed status/error handling unchanged. If a minimum completion count is needed for a decode comparison, state the threshold before comparing and report rows below it separately; never relabel them as full-cap samples.
- The official API path reviewed here has no client-side `ignore_eos` support. Adding EOS suppression or a repeated continuation request would alter the API semantics and is not part of the minimum extension; it should be a separately reviewed method change, not smuggled into the stock comparison.
- Retain individual rows, median, range, and sample count for each separate input/output setting. Keep failed requests, skipped tests, short EOS completions, and cached rows explicit; do not turn them into successful full-length samples.

## Test separation

No tests were run in this research task. If the proposed extension is later implemented, add narrowly scoped offline CLI/parameter-plumbing tests: defaults preserve the current 32768/24 behavior; explicit values reach only the selected `--long` case; result metadata records the selected values; unrelated 4K/16K and agent settings remain unchanged; streamed finish reason and actual usage completion count are preserved. Keep those tests separate from any HTTP/GPU benchmark. Do not use an agent-test invocation as speed evidence. Run the unchanged `bench.sh` benchmark for measurements only after the source extension is reviewed and installed in the same client worktree used by all arms.

## Source references

- `bench.sh:1-10` — official wrapper, argument passthrough.
- `tools/strata_bench.py:55-62,128-175,178-201,225-254,281-302,401-411,835-849,901-919` — fixed caps, request and aggregation path, calibrated prompt generation, long-case selection, CLI and recorded params.
- `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md:76-89` — documented stock suite and 32K long case.
- `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-fixed-history-logits-comparator-20261013/docs/MEASUREMENT_WORKFLOW.md` — shared-client comparison and sample/report rules.
